info.title: luma/ray-flash-2
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "luma/ray-flash-2", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: This model's input has not been narrowed by Comfy yet. Router forwards the body to the partner unchanged, so the partner's own documentation is authoritative until a schema is authored for this model. Any JSON object is accepted here and by the server's pre-provider validation alike.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Luma Dream Machine VIDEO models: the terminal `GET /proxy/luma/generations/{id}` document, forwarded unchanged. The submit is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `routerresult/classification.go` records `{provider: luma, endpoint: /generations}` as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll` — and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished generation rather than the `{id, state: queued}` handle the underlying submit answers with.
The generated video is at `assets.video`. The `luma/photon-*` IMAGE models answer on this same status route with a different document — the asset under `assets.image`, the video leaves null — so they carry a schema of their own rather than sharing this one; `routerpollstate.classifyLuma` accepts EITHER leaf as success, precisely so that a terminal success of one operation is not reported as an output-less failure by a rule written for the other.
`assets.progress_video` is NOT the result. Luma publishes it as an in-flight preview while the generation is still running, so a document carrying only that leaf is a completed generation that produced nothing — which `classifyLuma` answers as `success_without_output` rather than as a result, and which is why the SDK cases for this family assert the dotted leaf `assets.video` rather than the `assets` container.
`state` is Luma's own lowercase four-value vocabulary — `queued`, `dreaming` (Luma's word for in-progress), `completed`, `failed` — forwarded unchanged and compared without a case fold. `failure_reason` is populated only alongside `failed`.
The example below is a `luma/ray-2` VIDEO generation. `request` is omitted from it on purpose: it is any one of four request shapes and Router echoes back whichever one the caller sent — the `LumaGeneration` component this composes over carries a worked one of its own.

LumaAspectRatio.description: The aspect ratio of the generation

progress_video.description: The URL of the progress video

callback_url.description: The callback URL for the audio

negative_prompt.description: The negative prompt of the audio

request.prompt: A serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset

created_at.description: The date and time when the generation was created

failure_reason.description: The reason for the state of the generation

model.description: The model used for the generation

LumaGenerationRequestEcho.description: The video generation request, echoed back inside the terminal document. Luma serialises every field of its request model, writing an explicit `null` into each one the caller did not set, so read a field's presence from its VALUE rather than from the key.

callback_url.description: The callback URL of the generation

generation_type.description: Always `video` when set, echoing the operation. Null when the caller did not send one, for the reason this whole echo object exists.

LumaImageGenerationRequestEcho.description: The image generation request, echoed back inside the terminal document. Luma serialises every field of its request model, writing an explicit `null` into each one the caller did not set, so read a field's presence from its VALUE rather than from the key.

callback_url.description: The callback URL for the generation

identity0.description: The image identity, echoed back — null when the caller sent none

generation_type.description: Always `image` when set, echoing the operation. Null when the caller did not send one, for the reason this whole echo object exists.

LumaImageIdentityEcho.description: An image identity as it comes BACK inside the terminal document. Same shape as `LumaImageIdentity`, with its members nullable for the reason `LumaImageRefEcho` gives.

images.description: The URLs of the image identity

LumaImageModel.description: The image model used for the generation

LumaImageRefEcho.description: An image reference as it comes BACK inside the terminal document. Same shape as `LumaImageRef`, with each member nullable because Luma echoes an unset one as an explicit `null` rather than omitting it.

url.description: The URL of the image reference

weight.description: The weight of the image reference

LumaKeyframe.description: A keyframe can be either a Generation reference, an Image, or a Video

LumaModifyImageRefEcho.description: A modify-image reference as it comes BACK inside the terminal document. Same shape as `LumaModifyImageRef`, with its members nullable for the reason `LumaImageRefEcho` gives.

url.description: The URL of the image reference

weight.description: The weight of the modify image reference

callback_url.description: The callback URL for the upscale

LumaVideoModel.description: The video model used for the generation
